syntheses.title: Comparison of Autonomous Driving Methods in CARLA Simulator and ChauffeurNet Studies
syntheses.body: Paper A compares three autonomous driving approaches using the CARLA simulator: classic modular pipeline, end-to-end imitation learning, and end-to-end reinforcement learning, noting that modular pipeline and imitation learning performance differ by less than 10% (claims 34863bb0-827c-5405-a15d-f7229ca8985c, 32a49fa0-8395-506b-9794-efc1f7fa2a8f). Paper B reports findings on pure imitation learning, highlighting its limitations in driving tasks despite high-capacity models and large datasets (claims 09081b52-e1ad-5843-9bbc-8565cf5aea59, 639f88c8-001d-587a-bae9-390fb3c89dcf). Thus, the studies collectively compare imitation learning with modular pipeline and note challenges in pure imitation learning approaches.
